newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - First International estimate up.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - First International estimate up.

text.p: Lehman Brothers raised its 1997 earnings estimate for First International Bank of Israel after better-than-expected third quarter results but said the stock is fully valued.
The bank "appears to have had a strong third quarter and when compared with the weaker Q3 1995 the result has been to sharply improve year-to-year comparisons," analyst Ian McEwen wrote in a report.
He forecast fourth-quarter net income of 45 million shekels after a nine-month result of 130 million.
"Our estimate for the full year 1996 of 175 million shekels implying earnings per share (EPS) of 35 shekels appears realistic," the report said.

"On the other hand our 1997 estimate does appear too low given that the benefits to interest surplus are likely to be fairly sustainable. We have raised our forecast for 1997 to 185 million, equivalent to EPS of 36.5 and a return on equity held around nine percent," the report said.
